To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the NBTI induced by exceptional negative bias is characterized by a very fast initial degradation and a very slow recovery, (ii) the recovery is strongly dependent on the gate voltage, the temperature and the time duration of the stress, and (iii) the recovery is characterized by an exponential behavior.
exceptional operative gate voltage induces positive charge trapping in the gate oxide and this charge can induce threshold voltage instability.

1) Exceptional negative gate voltage can induce large threshold shift on n-type DMOS transistor; 2) Positive charge trapping is responsible of the threshold shift; 3) The effect is still present even during the standard operative conditions.

the study of NBTI in the case of exceptional negative bias, in particular the study of the recovery process.
the investigation of NBTI effect on n-type trench devices and the related reliability issue in automotive applications.

the effect of the exceptional negative bias is a serious reliability problem that should not be ignored.
